issues.message: Image element missing text alternative (content description)
issues.wcag_description: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for the situations listed below.
issues.why_it_matters: Screen readers need text alternatives to describe images and other non-text content to visually impaired users. Without proper alternatives, users who cannot see the content will miss important information.
issues.how_to_fix: Add alt text to images, provide descriptions for icons, and ensure all visual content has text equivalents. Use contentDescription attribute in Android for images.

issues.wcag_description: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
issues.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies need to understand the structure and relationships between content elements to properly convey information to users with disabilities.
issues.how_to_fix: Use proper semantic HTML, ensure proper heading structure, and use ARIA labels when needed. In mobile, use proper view hierarchies and accessibility properties.

issues.wcag_description: The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, except for large text, incidental text, or logotypes.
issues.why_it_matters: Low contrast text is difficult to read for users with low vision or in bright lighting conditions, making content inaccessible.
issues.how_to_fix: Increase contrast ratio between text and background to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt+bold).

issues.why_it_matters: Assistive technologies need to understand what each component is, what it does, and its current state to properly interact with it.
issues.how_to_fix: Use proper semantic HTML and ARIA attributes when necessary. Ensure custom components have proper accessibility properties.

issues.message: Clickable element has no visible label or content description
issues.wcag_description: All interactive elements must have accessible names that describe their purpose and can be programmatically determined.
issues.why_it_matters: Screen reader users cannot interact with elements that have no labels, making functionality completely inaccessible.
issues.how_to_fix: Add visible text labels or content descriptions to all interactive elements. Use accessibilityLabel in iOS and contentDescription in Android.

issues.wcag_description: Images that convey meaning must have text alternatives that serve the same purpose and convey the same information.
issues.why_it_matters: Visually impaired users need text descriptions to understand image content and context that would otherwise be missed.
issues.how_to_fix: Add alt text to informative images and mark decorative images as such. Use empty alt text for decorative images.

issues.message: Clickable elements overlap and may cause touch errors
issues.wcag_description: Interactive elements must not overlap in ways that cause accidental activation or confusion about which element will be activated.
issues.why_it_matters: Overlapping elements cause accidental touches and navigation errors, frustrating users and making the interface unpredictable.
issues.how_to_fix: Ensure adequate spacing between interactive elements. Maintain clear visual separation between clickable areas.

issues.wcag_description: The purpose of each button can be determined from its text or from the context in which it appears.
issues.why_it_matters: Users need to understand what will happen when they activate a button to make informed decisions and avoid unexpected results.
issues.how_to_fix: Use descriptive button text that clearly indicates the action. Avoid vague labels like 'Submit' or 'Click Here'.
